items.claim: The speaker shift the front seam rests on and the closing-formula recurrence both hold in the bytes, and the span owes no scribal-layer disclosure.
items.evidence: Both spliced runs match the source bytes of the verses they cite, at byte tier: שְׁמוּעָ֤ה שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.49.14, byte tier) and לֹֽא יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן אָדָֽם (oshb:Jer.49.18, byte tier). The seam warrant is byte-attested rather than translation-borne: 49:13 carries the oath verb נִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי֙ (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte tier) with the deity as its subject, while 49:14 opens with a first-person verb whose subject is the reporting prophet and which names the deity separately as the source in the following prepositional phrase; the two first-person forms differ in subject referent, not merely in English voicing. The identity claim on the closing clause was re-tested by exact codepoint comparison and holds: the nine-token run is identical codepoint for codepoint at 49:18, 49:33 and 50:40, and the consonantal sweep for that run returns exactly those three verses (sweep: 3 verses), so the three named sites are the complete set and the disclosure is not selective. No parashah, paseq or variant entry falls at 49:13 through 49:18, so nothing is owed under span-relevant symmetry; the span is Hebrew throughout with no language-island exposure, and every cited coordinate lies outside the one renumbering zone. Non-blocking residual: the parashah segment running from after 49:11 to after 49:19 crosses this unit's own back seam at 49:18|49:19 unstated, though that layer is tier-3 weak, single-witness and never a boundary driver, and the mark itself is disclosed at the adjacent span.
tier_citations: codepoint-identity comparison across oshb:Jer.49.18, oshb:Jer.49.33, oshb:Jer.50.40

items.claim: The stated grammatical ground for disregarding the setumah recorded at 49:19 is contradicted by the verse bytes.
items.evidence: The rationale holds that the lion simile's rhetorical questions continue grammatically past 49:19 into 49:20-21 and that the sentence the mark falls inside runs past the verse boundary. The bytes say otherwise: the question series כִּ֣י מִ֤י כָמ֨וֹנִי֙ וּמִ֣י יֹעִידֶ֔נִּי וּמִי זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽי (oshb:Jer.49.19, byte tier) closes inside 49:19 at the verse-final accent, and 49:20 opens a fresh independent clause with לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ (oshb:Jer.49.20, byte tier), a consequential particle plus imperative, with 49:21 a further independent clause. The disposition itself survives, since a single-witness tier-3 mark never drives a boundary and both marks here are correctly typed setumah at 49:19 and 49:22, but the warrant has to be restated on discourse dependence rather than on a sentence that both the accents and the verse division end. Secondary: the cross-oracle recurrence is asserted with no tier. Re-checked against the source bytes, the first seven tokens of 49:19 are codepoint-identical to the first seven of 50:44, and the first six of 49:20 to the first six of 50:45, each construction standing at exactly two verses (sweep: 2 verses each) - stronger than stated, but still untiered as written, and the parallel passage additionally carries a variant note that 49:19 does not.
tier_citations: codepoint-identity comparison against oshb:Jer.50.44 and oshb:Jer.50.45

items.claim: The 49:25 variant note is misidentified, the header is called a different shape from neighbours it in fact matches, and an in-span paseq goes undisclosed.
items.evidence: 49:25 reads אֵ֥יךְ לֹֽא עֻזְּבָ֖ה עִ֣יר תהלה תְּהִלָּ֑ת קִרְיַ֖ת מְשׂוֹשִֽׂי (oshb:Jer.49.25, byte tier): the variant pair sits on the praise noun, unpointed ketiv beside the pointed qere in construct, and the verse carries no demonstrative anywhere, so a variant note on the demonstrative is byte-false. The header לְדַמֶּ֗שֶׂק (oshb:Jer.49.23, byte tier) is the same lamed-plus-nation shape as לִבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֗וֹן (oshb:Jer.49.1, byte tier), לֶאֱד֗וֹם (oshb:Jer.49.7, byte tier) and לְקֵדָ֣ר (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier), four of the six lamed-initial nation headers in this book; what actually differs is the missing speech formula, which the same sentence states correctly, so calling the header a different shape mislabels a form class the substrate keeps separate. The formula absence itself checks out: the koh-amar construction stands nowhere in 49:23 through 49:27 (sweep: 0 verses in span, against 153 verses book-wide). Disclosure is asymmetric: the setumah entries keyed to 49:22 and 49:27 are correctly typed and the 49:25 variant is named, but the paseq recorded at 49:24 falls inside this span and goes unmentioned while the same count-only layer is disclosed at 49:28, 49:37 and 49:39 in adjacent spans; neither setumah citation carries the single-witness label that the paseq citations elsewhere do carry.
tier_citations: byte (pointed splices, oshb:Jer.49.25 / oshb:Jer.49.23 / oshb:Jer.49.1 / oshb:Jer.49.7 / oshb:Jer.49.28)

items.claim: The header verse is described as dating a coming strike, which its perfect verb, both witnesses' renderings and the book's date-site classification all contradict.
items.evidence: 49:28 reads אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִכָּה֙ נבוכדראצור נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier): a perfect verb in a retrospective relative clause identifying the target, rendered “which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck” (web:Jer.49.28). No year, reign or month element stands in the verse, and it does not appear among the book's nineteen classified date-candidate sites (sweep: 19 classified verses, 49:28 not among them); the classified sites inside this oracle block are 46:2 and 51:59, and the dating nearest this chapter is the accession clause at 49:34, itself a separate form object. Both the coming-strike reading and the dated-header type label carry that error. The variant work is otherwise byte-correct and re-verifies here: the ketiv is the plene byform נבוכדראצור standing unpointed beside the qere נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר in the same verse (both oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier), the added vav does fall before the final resh, that spelling stands at exactly one verse (sweep: 1 verse) against the resh-family spelling at twenty-nine (sweep: 29 verses) including 49:30 and 50:17, and at 49:30 the ketiv עליהם is corrected by the qere עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם (both oshb:Jer.49.30, byte tier), exactly the against-them to against-you shift claimed. Paseq count one at 49:28 with the single-witness label, and the front-seam setumah at 49:27, both check out; the formula quoted from this verse is the divine one in its own mouth, with no embedded-speech ownership question at this site. Residual: the sole-site wording is an exclusivity claim shipped without its own digit-bearing sweep, although the underlying fact holds at one verse.

items.claim: The front seam is defended with evidence located two verses earlier and against this unit's own stated segmentation, and carries high confidence that no device at the seam supports.
items.evidence: The discriminators named, the change of target to Hazor and the renewed flight command, both stand at 49:30: נֻסוּ֩ נֻּ֨דוּ מְאֹ֜ד הֶעְמִ֧יקוּ לָשֶׁ֛בֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֥י חָצ֖וֹר (oshb:Jer.49.30, byte tier). The same sentence assigns Hazor the block 49:30 through 49:33, which this cut then divides at 49:31|49:32. At the seam actually taken the substrate offers nothing: no parashah entry falls between the setumah after 49:27 and the setumah after 49:33, no paseq or variant note falls at 49:31 or 49:32, and no formula onset opens 49:32. What does stand at the seam is a shift the opening sentence denies: 49:31 is second-person plural imperative address to the attackers, ק֣וּמוּ עֲל֗וּ (oshb:Jer.49.31, byte tier), echoing ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier) and bracketing 49:28 through 49:31, while 49:32 drops to third-person report with no addressee. Either that is an addressee shift, contradicting the claim that the spoils continue without one, or the seam carries no device at all; on neither reading does high confidence hold. Verified correct: the closing clause at 49:33 is codepoint-identical to 49:18 and 50:40 (oshb:Jer.49.33, byte tier; sweep: 3 verses), and the setumah keyed to 49:33 is correctly typed.
tier_citations: codepoint-identity comparison across oshb:Jer.49.18, oshb:Jer.49.33, oshb:Jer.50.40

items.claim: The date-frame gloss carries the long royal-name form where the verse writes the short one, and the rejected alternative contradicts this unit's own reading of the header's content.
items.evidence: 49:34 writes בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַלְכ֛וּת צִדְקִיָּ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.49.34, byte tier) - the short royal-name form, attested at four verses in this book (sweep: 4 verses) against forty-four for the long form - while the transliteration renders it in the long form twice, inside a claim whose whole value is byte-exact form discrimination, in a book where that name's spelling split is a live hazard class. Separately, the rejected alternative states that the header carries no content of its own apart from the judgment that immediately follows; the same verse's dating clause is content of its own, and the rationale itself treats that clause as the header's distinguishing feature. The declared heuristic disposition on that flagged sentence therefore does not hold: the wording is substantively inconsistent with this unit's own analysis, not merely a phrase match. Everything else re-verifies: the opening אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל עֵילָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.49.34, byte tier) is one of exactly four sites of that nations-header shape (sweep: 4 verses); the accession construct stands at one verse only (sweep: 1 verse) and is indeed a different noun form from the three sites using the other construct spelling; the 49:36 variant is on the nation name, unpointed ketiv עולם beside pointed qere עֵילָֽם (both oshb:Jer.49.36, byte tier); paseq count two at 49:37 with the single-witness label; the front-seam setumah at 49:33 is correctly typed; and all three splices reach byte tier.

items.claim: The variant pair is labelled a verb pair the bytes make a noun, and the parashah entry adduced for the front seam sits on the far side of the unit.
items.evidence: 49:39 reads וְהָיָ֣ה בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים אשוב אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת שבית שְׁב֥וּת עֵילָ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.49.39, byte tier). The second pair stands immediately after the object marker אֶת and is the noun that verb governs, not a verb; the same construction at 49:6, אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת שְׁב֥וּת בְּנֵֽי עַמּ֖וֹן (oshb:Jer.49.6, byte tier), shows it unambiguously, so calling both pairs the idiom's own two verbs is a form-class claim the bytes refuse. The mark evidence points the wrong way: the setumah keyed to 49:39 trails that verse and closes the Elam block, so it cannot corroborate the boundary between the coda and the judgment material preceding it; the front seam at 49:38|49:39 carries no entry in any layer, and the 49:6 parallel invoked has the identical geometry, its mark following 49:6 with none at 49:5. Nor does the closure formula ending 49:38 license the cut under the ruled treatment of that formula as closure corroboration only where a fresh first-tier onset follows: וְהָיָ֣ה בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.49.39, byte tier) is a temporal pivot, not one of the onset classes. The content pivot from judgment to restoration is real, but high confidence overstates a seam with no device on it. Verified correct: two variant notes at 49:39 and paseq count one with the single-witness label; the comparison digits are right at two notes for 50:6 and four for 50:11, though a four-note verse is not itself a doubled-note site as the sentence implies; and all five spliced runs reach byte tier. Residual: the 49:6 idiom is invoked with no quoted form and no tier, and that contiguous construction stands at four verses (sweep: 4 verses).

items.claim: Gloss extent and splice extent diverge on the second Hebrew run, and the one scribal layer cited at the front seam is left silent where it crosses the back seam.
items.evidence: The English quotation runs through the first god-name while the splice אִמְרוּ֩ נִלְכְּדָ֨ה בָבֶ֜ל (oshb:Jer.50.2, byte tier) stops at the city name and additionally carries the imperative אִמְרוּ֩, which the gloss does not render; the god-name material quoted sits in the following words הֹבִ֥ישׁ בֵּל֙ (oshb:Jer.50.2, byte tier), outside the splice. The gloss therefore covers what the splice does not and the splice covers what the gloss does not. On disclosure, the setumah keyed to 49:39 is correctly cited for the front seam, but the next entry in that layer falls after 50:5, so the segment opening at 50:1 runs straight across this unit's own back seam at 50:3|50:4 unstated - the same weak single-witness layer used one way at one seam and left silent at the other. Minor: the nations header at 49:34 opens its unit and closes nothing, so describing it as just closed at 49:34 misplaces it; and the sentence carrying the 49:39 disclosure is malformed. Verified correct: the opening הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל בָּבֶ֖ל (oshb:Jer.50.1, byte tier) is the davar-asher-dibber shape, distinct from the three word-event shapes and from the 49:34 header, with that contiguous construction at three verses (sweep: 3 verses); the summons splice הַגִּ֨ידוּ בַגּוֹיִ֤ם וְהַשְׁמִ֨יעוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.50.2, byte tier) matches its gloss exactly; the parent named is the twelve-frame nations parent rather than a Babylon-only collection, so the Babylon oracle's continuation past this unit is not treated as a parent seam; and the declared heuristic disposition on the no-scene-change wording holds, since 50:1 through 50:3 is one scene with no participant change in the bytes.
